transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. Um, I hope I'm doing this right, but... I guess I'm here because of some family stress. I really don't want to sound like a difficult person or like I'm just complaining, because I know every family has their little issues, right? 

But... well, it's about my husband's sister. For a little over a year now, she's been sort of... working the family business, I guess you could say. Just quietly trying to get control of the money and push me out of any decisions. And, you know, folks try to smooth it over and tell me it's nothing, and I always try to be agreeable and keep the peace, I really do. But I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.

When your family members tell you that the sister isn't actually trying to push you out, do you find their explanations convincing, or do you remain certain that something is really going on despite what they say?

Oh, well... I really try to listen to them, I truly do. I don't want to be stubborn or, you know, cause any rifts for my husband. I know they're just trying to keep everyone happy. But... um... I hope it's okay to just be completely honest with you here. 

No matter how folks try to smooth it over, I just... I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. I don't want to call my family liars, but I can see exactly how she's working things to get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. 

I hate to sound so negative about it, I really do. I usually just smile and nod when they tell me I'm worrying over nothing, because I don't want to upset anyone or make a scene. Does that make me sound awful? I just can't pretend I don't see what's happening, even if I wish it wasn't. Am I explaining that alright?

When you observe your sister-in-law working with the family business and the money, are you seeing or hearing things that others around you don't seem to notice, or is it more that you're interpreting her actions and words differently than your family does?

Oh, no, I'm not... I'm not seeing things that aren't there, or hearing voices or anything like that. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm losing my mind, because I promise I'm not. I'm just... I'm just seeing what she does. 

Like, the way she talks to the accountants, or how she always manages to schedule the important meetings when she knows I'm busy with the grandkids. It's just normal things she does, but... well, I guess I just see what it all adds up to, and my husband and the others just see a helpful sister. They think she's just pitching in, but I can see the pattern, you know? 

I really try not to make a fuss about it, and I'd never want you to think I'm making up stories or seeing things. I just... I just notice the little things she does differently than they do. Is that... is that a normal way to explain it? I hope I'm making sense.

If you saw clear evidence that your sister-in-law's actions were genuinely helpful and not part of a plan to push you out, do you think you could accept that and change your mind, or do you feel certain that no matter what evidence appeared, she would still be working against you?

Oh, my... I would really love to be wrong, Doctor. I truly would. I'd love nothing more than to just get along and find out I was mistaken about the whole thing, because I really don't want to be a difficult person. 

But... um... honestly? Even if someone showed me something that looked like proof she was just helping... I just couldn't ignore what I already know. I came in today because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over or what they might try to show me, I just know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. 

I'm so sorry, I hope you don't think I'm just being awful or closed-minded for saying that. I just can't unsee what she's doing, even if I wish I could. Am I answering your question the right way?

When you think about why your sister-in-law is doing all this—trying to get control of the money and push you out—what do you think her ultimate goal or reason is? What is she actually trying to accomplish in the end?

Oh, gosh... well, I don't really know for sure. I try not to assume the worst about people, I really do. I don't want to sit around thinking up terrible motives for her, because that just feels so... well, so uncharitable, doesn't it? 

I guess... um... I'm not really sure what her grand plan is at the end of the day. Maybe she just wants to feel important, or maybe she thinks she knows best? I don't really know what's in her heart. I just see what she's doing with the meetings and the money, but I couldn't tell you exactly why she feels the need to do it. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a better answer for that. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just... I really haven't figured out the "why" of it all. Does that make sense? I'm trying my best to give you good answers.

When your sister-in-law does these things—like scheduling meetings when you're busy or talking to the accountants in certain ways—do you think she's deliberately doing them to target you specifically, or could some of these things just be coincidences that happen to work out that way?

Oh, dear... I really wish I could just say it was all a big coincidence. I try so hard to tell myself that, I really do. I'll think to myself, 'Well, she probably just forgot I had the grandkids today,' because I don't want to be the sort of person who thinks people are out to get them. That just sounds so... well, so bitter, doesn't it? And I promise I'm not a bitter person. 

But... it just happens so often now. I don't know if she sits down and deliberately plans to target me specifically, like... like someone in a television show. I really hope she doesn't. It just... it really feels like it's aimed at me, even when I try my hardest to give her the benefit of the doubt. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound awful to say that. Is it okay that I feel that way? I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around looking for things to be upset about.

When your sister-in-law schedules those meetings when you're busy or talks to the accountants in certain ways, do you think she's actively thinking about you and trying to interfere with you specifically, or do you think she's just going about her business and these things happen to affect you as a side effect?

Oh, goodness... I know I must sound like a broken record, and I really hope you're not getting frustrated with me. I'm trying so hard to explain it right. 

I guess... well, I don't really know if she's sitting there actively thinking about me every single second. I'd like to think she's just going about her business and maybe she's just a bit thoughtless? That sounds much nicer, doesn't it? Just someone being a little careless, rather than someone being mean on purpose. 

But... oh, I don't know. It's just hard to believe it's only a side effect when it keeps happening over and over, you know? But I really couldn't say for sure exactly what's going through her head. I'm sorry, I know that's not a very clear answer. Am I being helpful at all? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

When you look back over this past year, do you see all of these things your sister-in-law has done as part of one big plan she's been working on, or do they feel more like separate incidents that just happen to be upsetting?

Oh, my... well, I really try not to look at it as some big, awful scheme. That just sounds so dramatic, doesn't it? Like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill. I always try to tell myself, 'Oh, this is just one little thing, and that was just another little thing.' 

I really don't want to be the kind of person who thinks someone is spending a whole year plotting against them. That would make me sound a bit... well, a bit paranoid, wouldn't it? And I promise you, I'm not like that. 

So, I try to just see them as separate little incidents. Just... just bumps in the road, really. Even if there are quite a lot of bumps lately. I just think it's better to look at it that way, rather than imagining some grand plan. Does that seem like a reasonable way to look at it? I hope I'm answering these questions the right way for you.

When you think about everything your sister-in-law has done over this past year—the meetings, the conversations with accountants, all of it—do you believe these are all connected as part of one deliberate plan she's carrying out against you, or do you think they're mostly unrelated things that just happen to be frustrating?

Oh, goodness, I... I know we were just talking about this, and I hope I'm not confusing you or making things difficult. I really don't want to be a bother. 

I... well, like I was saying, I try so hard to just think of them as unrelated things. Just separate, frustrating little moments. Because if I start thinking they're all connected into one big, deliberate plan... well, that just sounds terrible, doesn't it? It sounds like I'm accusing her of being some sort of evil mastermind, and I really, really don't want to be that kind of person. I want to be fair and kind.

So, I try to just tell myself they're unrelated. I mean, I don't know for absolute certain what's in her heart, but I think it's just better to look at it as separate things. That's the right way to handle it, don't you think? I hope that makes sense... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.

If I asked your husband or other family members right now, 'Does your sister-in-law have a plan to push your wife out and take control of the money?', what do you think they would say, and do you believe they would be wrong?

Oh, dear... well, if you asked my husband or the rest of the family, they'd probably just say, 'Oh, she's just being helpful,' or 'You're misunderstanding her intentions.' They... they really try to smooth it all over, you know? They want everyone to just get along, which is lovely, it really is. I want everyone to get along, too.

But... oh, I hope this doesn't make me sound stubborn, but... yes, I do think they'd be wrong. I mean, I came in here today because... well, because I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. She's been working this family business in a way that... well, it really seems like she's trying to get control of the money and push me out of making any decisions. 

I know they don't want to see it that way, and I feel terrible even saying it out loud because it sounds so uncharitable. I really try to be a good, forgiving person. But no matter how much they try to brush it under the rug, I just can't ignore what's happening right in front of me. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think poorly of me for disagreeing with my family about this. I just have to be honest with you, don't I?

When you think about everything your sister-in-law is doing with the business and the money, does it all fit together into one clear, logical explanation of what she's trying to accomplish, or does it feel more scattered and hard to piece together into a complete picture?

Oh, gosh... I really couldn't say if it all fits together perfectly into one clear explanation. I mean, I certainly don't sit around trying to map it all out like some kind of detective. That would make me sound a bit crazy, wouldn't it? 

I think... well, it feels much more scattered to me. I'm not the most educated person, you know, I didn't finish high school, so I definitely don't pretend to understand all the complicated business things she does. To me, it's just a bunch of confusing, frustrating moments that don't really make a complete picture. I just know what I see, and it feels like I'm being pushed to the side, even if I can't explain the exact logic of how she's doing it. 

I'm sorry, I wish I had a clearer answer for you. I just try not to dwell on it too much so I don't get myself all worked up. Is that an okay answer? I really hope I'm being helpful to you.

Have you ever experienced anything unusual with your senses—like hearing voices or sounds that others don't hear, or seeing things that others don't see, or noticing strange smells, tastes, or feelings on your skin that seem out of place?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I mean, I know some people struggle with those sorts of things, and my heart goes out to them, it really does, but... no, my hearing is perfectly fine, and my eyesight too—well, except for needing my reading glasses, of course! 

I've never heard voices or seen anything strange. And no odd smells or feelings on my skin either. I'm just a very normal, boring person when it comes to all of that. I hope that's the right answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm making things up or imagining things that aren't there. I'm very grounded in reality, I promise.
If you're being completely honest with yourself, deep down, do you have any real doubt that your sister-in-law is trying to push you out and control the money, or are you absolutely certain about it?

Oh, my... well, I really wish I could say I wasn't sure. It would be so much nicer if I was just mistaken, wouldn't it? I hate sounding so stubborn, I really do. I always try to see the good in everyone, and I don't want you to think I'm just a suspicious or mean-spirited person. 

But... if I'm being completely honest with you, like you asked... no, I don't have any real doubt. I'm certain. I mean, that's really why I came in to see you. My husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over or make excuses for her, I just... I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. 

I just can't pretend it isn't happening, even though it breaks my heart. Is it awful of me to say I'm absolutely certain about something so unpleasant? I really hope you understand where I'm coming from, and that I'm just trying to give you the most truthful answer I can.

If you woke up tomorrow and somehow had absolute proof—like documents or recordings—that your sister-in-law was genuinely just helping the family business and had no plan against you at all, do you think you could accept that proof and change your mind completely, or would you find a way to explain away that proof?

Oh, goodness... that's a very hard question, Doctor. I really want to be the kind of person who could just... look at a piece of paper and say, "Oh, I was wrong, thank heavens!" I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just some stubborn, difficult woman who won't listen to reason. 

But... well, if I'm being perfectly honest... I don't think I could just accept it. I mean, I know what I've been living through for over a year now. I've watched her working this family business, maneuvering things so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. If someone handed me a document saying otherwise, I'd just... well, I'd probably think she faked it. Or that she tricked whoever made the recording. She's very smart, you know? Much smarter than me with all her education. 

I know that sounds terrible, and I'm so sorry if that makes me seem unreasonable. I just... I know what I've seen with my own two eyes, no matter how folks try to smooth it over. Does that make sense? I hope you're not disappointed in me for saying that. I just want to be truthful with you.
